title: VPC Service Controls Perimeter Violations

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:pubsub:message` events with `protoPayload.serviceName="accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com"` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.23 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:pubsub:message` traffic without `protoPayload.serviceName="accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com"`. Confirm UC-4.3.23 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.3.23 — VPC Service Controls Perimeter Violations: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:pubsub:message` for search criteria `protoPayload.serviceName="accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, 'VPC Service Controls Perimeter Violations' highlights abnormal network flow patterns—reconnaissance, lateral movement, or blocked exfiltration that perimeter tools may not correlate across cloud segments. UC-4.3.23 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable VPC SC violation logging. Forward to Pub/Sub and Splunk. Alert on every violation. Correlate with principal, source IP, and resource. Use for perimeter tuning and incident response.
visualization: Table (principal, resource, violation), Timeline (violations), Map (source IPs).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable VPC SC violation logging. Forward to Pub/Sub and Splunk. Alert on every violation. Correlate with principal, source IP, and resource. Use for perimeter tuning and incident response.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" protoPayload.serviceName="accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.23_vpc_service_controls_per_23"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect vpc service controls perimeter violations. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_23_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (principal, resource, violation), Timeline (violations), Map (source IPs)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of vpc service controls perimeter violations so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
